RACING RECAP O6/20/2015
VANSTRATEN OUTDUELS
CZARAPATA AS STOCK CARS TAKEI
CENTERSTAGE
By: Scott Owen
Shawano,WI 6/20/15—Travis VanStraten passed Brandon Czarapata with two laps remaining to win his 6th feature of the year
and take home the $750 top prize. Nick Anvelink won his 4th straight and 5th late model feature of the season. Jerry Wilinski
scored his 2nd IMCA Modified feature, Lucas Lamberies won his 2nd straight IMCA Sport Modified, and Grant Kastning also won
his 2nd Might Four feature.
Mark Rose led the opening lap of the Late Model feature before Jared Siefert asserted himself as the leader. In only his second
night at the track in a late model the former IMCA Modified track champion quickly pulled away from the rest of the pack while
Brett Swedberg and Troy Springborn gave chase. Meanwhile I2th place starter Nick Anvelink began to work his way through traffic.
The first caution of the race waved after lap thirteen wiping away the huge lead that Siefert had built up. As the race went back
to green it was Siefert leading Springborn, Swedberg, and Anvelink. Anvelink then passed both Swedberg and Springborn in turns
three and four to grab second. With Siefert still leading Anvelink set his sights on the leader. On lap seventeen Anvelink went to
the outside of Siefert and took the lead by a fender at the start finish line. Anvelink quickly pulled away from Siefert and went on
to win the race. Siefert finished second, Springborn took third, Swedberg finished fourth.
One day after turning 58 years old Art Siefert celebrated his birthday by taking the lead on the opening lap of the IMCA Modified
feature. Siefert immediately began to receive pressure from Joel Seegert. Jamie Schmidt raced his way to second on lap 4. The
following lap saw Schmidt make contact with Seifert bringing out a caution. Siefert would get his spot back, while Schmidt would
be sent to the tail of the field. As the race went back to green on lap 5 Jerry Wilinski made the pass on Siefert to take the lead.
Wilinski would lead the rest of the race for the win. Siefert held off John Peters to finish second equaling his son Jared's effort.
Marcus Yarie passed Seegert in the late stages of the race to finish fourth.
Josh Mroczkowski led laps one and two of the IMCA Stock car feature before Mike Schmidt took the lead on lap three. Rod
Snellenberger, Brandon Czarapata, Travis VanStraten and Shawn Wagner quickly joined the lead duo in a six car battle at the front of
the field. On lap four Czarapata went three wide with Schmidt and Mroczkowski and took the lead. By lap six it was Czarapata out
front trailed by Snellenberger and VanStraten. As the race ran on the top three cars raced in a tight pack with VanStraten running
door to door with Snellenberger for numerous laps right on the back bumper of Czarapata. A caution on lap thirteen bunched the
field up. Czarapata got a good restart and held the lead. On lap seventeen Snellenberger pulled into the pits eliminating him from
competition. Mike Schmidt joined Czarapata and VanStraten in the top three. On lap eighteen VanStraten moved to the inside of
Czarapata and the pair raced side by side for two laps with Cazarapata holding the lead each lap by a fender. On lap twenty four
VanStraten again went under Czarapata and this time nudged ahead of Czarapata by a fender as the pair took the white flag. Enter-
ing turn one VanStraten drove in deeper than Czarapata and slid up the track into the high groove. VanStraten held off Czarapata
through turns three and four to win the race. Mike Schmidt took third, Shawn Wagner fourth, Dustin Loberger finished fifth and
took home the hard charger award after starting 18th.
The IMCA Sport Mod feature saw Greg Magsam lead the first three laps before being overtaken by Lucas Lamberies. Lamberies
fought off challenges first from Wyatt Block, then from Brock Saunders to win the race. Saunders would finish second. Jake Solin
took third. Jason Jach finished fourth after starting fourteenth.
Grant Kastning took the lead from Aaron Milavitz on lap three of the Mighty Four feature and held off Lukas Hacker to win the
race. Brad Wedde crossed the line in third.
